posts.title: Youth are the future of innovation for our climate and oceans. By supporting our youth as leaders of digital transformation a
posts.caption:
Youth are the future of innovation for our climate and oceans. By supporting our youth as leaders of digital transformation and climate action, we can strengthen our communities at their foundations and build the next generation of leaders and innovators.
 
The global Youth4Climate Initiative has released a call for innovative ideas for young people and youth organizations to take climate action, with grants up to 20,000 USD alongside mentorship and capacity-building. There are four thematic areas: food and agriculture ,energy, education and urban sustainability. Apply here by March 31st, and please share with your communities 👉https://lnkd.in/dgC6nHia
 
Youth4Climate brings together existing and new online and offline resources, tools, capacities, partnerships, networks, and movements by and for youth, with a strong focus on implementation, for more sustained impact on climate on the ground. You can also register to the Youth4Climate Platform here 👉https://lnkd.in/dYfG24Dk

posts.title: 🌍 Inspired by the Youth4Climate: #SparkingSolutions Event Last week, I had the privilege of being part of the selection panel
posts.caption:
🌍 Inspired by the Youth4Climate: #SparkingSolutions Event
 
Last week, I had the privilege of being part of the selection panel for the Energy thematic at the Youth4Climate: Sparking Solutions event in Rome. Witnessing the passion, dedication, and innovative spirit of the youth presenting their energy projects was truly remarkable.
 
Gathering from 63 countries, these young minds came together with a 100 youth-driven solutions, all with a shared goal of creating a meaningful impact on our planet. The level of creativity and thoughtfulness in their projects was truly impressive.
 
At the event, I had the honor of witnessing some incredible project pitches from the youth. These innovative solutions included ideas such as harnessing affordable and renewable heating sources like Biomass, a high-performing stove that can save up to 5 tons of CO2 emissions, and initiatives to promote the use of solar power in off-grid schools and community centres. These ideas are not only impressive but also represent tangible steps towards reducing our carbon footprint and promoting #cleanenergy solutions. It's a testament to their dedication and ingenuity.
 
Taking part in the #Youth4Climate event reaffirmed my conviction: the future of our planet is in the hands of the next generation, and they are ready to take on the challenge. But we need to empower them, provide the support they need, and enable them to implement  their ideas so that #sustainableenergy use becomes the norm, not the exception.
 
The #Youth4Climate initiative, co-led by the UNDP Rome Centre  and Ministero dell'Ambiente e della Sicurezza Energetica  funding, mentorship programs, and capacity-building opportunities, these young climate leaders will have the tools to turn their innovative ideas into reality.

#EnergyForDevelopment

posts.title: Delighted to have delivered a keynote at the Round Table Discussion, organized by ISA with the EU and SolarPower Europe, on t
posts.caption:
Delighted to have delivered a keynote at the Round Table Discussion, organized by ISA with the EU and SolarPower Europe, on transforming Africa through sustainable energy & partnerships, where I emphasized the urgent need to evolve our financing approach to address disparities in clean energy finance in Africa.

Currently, investments are unevenly distributed, with ten nations accounting for 90% of private energy infrastructure investment. This leaves annual financing needs for energy access initiatives far short of the required $25B USD to achieve the 2030 objectives. In 2024, an estimated $110B USD will be invested in energy across Africa, with $70B allocated to fossil fuels and only 35% to clean energy technologies.

In my address, I highlighted the three key levers for systemic transformation:

1. To shift the focus of finance at the national level, which still prioritizes risks to lenders over the greater risk that climate change poses to people & the planet.
2. Changing the macro-level financial system to facilitate access to capital in critical geographies and sectors.
3. Optimizing energy systems with AI-driven solutions to boost renewable energy investment where its needed most.

Around 60 million people in Africa 🌍access electricity via off-grid solutions, with 15 countries using distributed renewables in their electrification plans. Scaling renewable, decentralized, and affordable energy systems can drive inclusive development.

Establishing robust financial models and fostering public-private partnerships are key to unlocking the $200 billion annual investment needed by 2030 for Africa's energy, climate, and development goals.

#EnergyForDevelopment ⚡️

posts.caption:
Delighted to announce the release of our latest policy paper from UNDP  Sustainable Energy Hub: "Innovative Governance for Private Sector in Just Energy Transition."

This policy action brief highlights the crucial role of the private sector in achieving a truly just energy transition. It explores how effective, inclusive, and accountable governance can boost private sector involvement, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and promote social and economic equity.

With 685 million people still lacking electricity, renewable #energy progress on SDG7 targets lagging, and a substantial investment gap to meet the Paris Agreement's 1.5-degree target, unlocking private sector investment is essential— and effective governance is key to this transition.

Read the full paper to discover comprehensive policy insights and practical examples that empower the private sector through public policy actions and supportive governance structures.

posts.title: Excellent meeting with H.E. Honourable Hamada Moussa, Comoros' Minister of Energy, at the Africa Energy Forum to discuss how
posts.caption:
Excellent meeting with H.E. Honourable Hamada Moussa, Comoros' Minister of Energy, at the Africa Energy Forum to discuss how Comoros is diversifying its economy and strengthening its productive capacity through renewable energy.

Energy plays a crucial role in catalyzing the Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS (ABAS) - a renewed declaration to deliver meaningful change and resilience in Small Island Developing States.

UNDP is supporting Comoros' transition by developing policies and frameworks to tap into geothermal and other natural resources for sustainable energy.

Opportunities for scaling up in Comoros include:

1. Enhancing the deployment of sustainable technologies, such as minigrids and geothermal solutions.

2. Facilitating innovative financing and risk mitigation for SIDS to safeguard the blue economy and enhance clean energy transitions.

3. Employing AI and analytics to refine off-grid solutions and strengthen data-driven policy.

UNDP is committed to advancing partnerships and actions to accelerate a just Energy Revolution in SIDS for transformative development. ⚡️

posts.caption:

This initiative could significantly enhance access to financing for sustainable energy solutions in Kenya.

posts.title: Delighted to have participated in the HLPF side event on ‘Financing a Sustainable Energy Future,’ organized by @IRENA. I emph
posts.caption:
Delighted to have participated in the HLPF side event on ‘Financing a Sustainable Energy Future,’ organized by @IRENA. I emphasized the urgent need to transform our financing approaches to address the disparities in clean energy investments in developing countries. Key takeaways include:

* Attracting private investments through policy de-risking and creating bankable projects.
* Reforming financial structures with green bonds and concessional loans for high-risk regions.
* Leveraging AI and digital solutions for optimized energy systems and investment planning.
* Implementing holistic approaches for a just energy transition that integrate governance, gender equality, and climate justice.
* Accelerating concrete, country-specific investments and ensuring their viability.

UNDP  is committed to fostering international partnerships and leveraging innovative financial solutions to drive energy, climate, and development convergence. 💡

#EnergyForDevelopment⚡ #HLPF2024

posts.title: Excellent roundtable discussion at #HLPF2024 on a Just Energy Transition in a SIDS Context, organized by the government of Co
posts.caption:
Excellent roundtable discussion at #HLPF2024 on a Just Energy Transition in a SIDS Context, organized by the government of Comoros. 🇰🇲  I emphasized the opportunities to overcome existing challenges that hinder sustainable energy adoption in #SIDS 🏝️through innovative solutions:

- Utilizing innovative finance mechanisms, including thematic bonds, and Debt-for-Energy transactions, to provide effective financing for SIDS' just energy transition
- Enhancing policy, de-risking mechanisms and regulatory frameworks to promote greater uptake of renewables
- Connecting renewables with green and blue economies to support economic diversification
- Harnessing digital technologies and AI to develop informed energy resilience strategies and optimize off-grid solutions, transforming SIDS into 'digital islands’ 🏝️
- Creating an ecosystem enabling active private sector participation to boost renewable energy capacity, job creation & technology transfer

Energy is pivotal in achieving the ambitious goals of the ABAS declaration. As a key partner of SIDS, UNDP's approach goes beyond conventional project development and aims at amplifying exponentially the impact of sustainable energy systems transformation on the ground to actualize these outcomes – our strategy is not just about providing energy; it’s about catalyzing #EnergyForDevelopment. ⚡️

posts.title: Delighted to have participated in the ‘Let’s Talk Data’ event with experts from @worldbank, @universityofmichigan, and @UNDP.
posts.caption:
Delighted to have participated in the ‘Let’s Talk Data’ event with experts from @worldbank, @universityofmichigan, and @UNDP. 

I emphasized on the human angle of sustainable energy for development, and the need to go beyond collecting data, making these findings actionable for amplifying our impact on the ground:

* Energy poverty affects health, social inclusion, and economic opportunities. We must prioritize data and indicators that include social, environmental and development dimensions
* Open energy modeling tools need to better incorporate social and development factors beyond market dynamics. We must invest in data infrastructure to address urban-rural disparities, informal energy markets, economic transitions, and disaggregated demographic data.
* Effective energy policies and interventions require precise, actionable insights derived from high-resolution geospatial data and advanced analytics, enabling equitable interventions to ensure renewable energy benefits reach all communities, especially underserved areas

At @UNDP, our focus remains on leveraging technology and data combined with an integrated development approach to achieve #SDG7 🌍 

Learn more 👉🏼 hrea.isr.umich.edu/ 💡
Damilola Ogunbiyi Marco Gervasi Marcos Neto International Energy Agency (IEA) Agostino Inguscio

posts.caption:
The severe floods in Pakistan in 2022 damaged 22 power plants and caused outages and load shedding of up to 16 hours. 

In the face of severe climate change, we must leverage the power of digital technologies and innovation to ensure energy resilience and security. Here is how:

* Smart grids and AI-driven storage enhance grid stability, reliability, and efficiency
* Advanced analytics and smart meters optimize energy use, empowering consumers with real-time data for more efficient consumption and cost savings
* IoT and Digital Twins (DT) provide real-time monitoring and proactive maintenance, ensuring infrastructure resilience and rapid response to extreme weather events

We discuss these strategies focusing on energy security in the latest issue of Development Advocate Pakistan — read the publication for an excellent collection of articles and thought leadership 👉🏼

posts.title: An energy revolution is underway in Iran, positioning renewable energy at the forefront of the country’s energy supply. With
posts.caption:
An energy revolution is underway in Iran, positioning renewable energy at the forefront of the country’s energy supply.

With an ambitious target of installing 30 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030, Iran has a significant opportunity to address inequalities, support workers and industries, and promote economic diversification by catalyzing transformative change.

Our sessions in Tehran with high-level representatives from Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Energy led to a productive exchange of actionable strategies for advancing a just energy transition:

1.⁠ Develop regulatory frameworks, enhance skills training for workers, and create targeted support systems to ensure a just transition
2.⁠ ⁠Scale sustainable finance through supportive policies that unlock investment in renewables and enhance energy efficiency
3.⁠ ⁠Leverage digital innovation and AI to optimize systems and enable data-driven policymaking within broader socio-economic contexts

This journey will be driven by the convergence of digitalization, market development, policy, and governance. 💡

#EnergyForDevelopment ⚡️

posts.caption:
Delighted to have contributed to an inspiring session on The Road to COP29: Island Priorities for Baku hosted by @Island Innovation. It was an excellent opportunity to emphasize how the energy transition in #SIDS can build resilience and unlock economic opportunities while discussing the key role of youth, and actionable steps to drive this shift: 

1.⁠ ⁠Establish a finance framework that provides debt relief & removes financial barriers, utilizing innovative tools like debt-for-energy swaps
2.⁠ ⁠Harness digital transformation to improve data availability, enabling infrastructure deployment and management tailored to each island community 
3.⁠ ⁠Implement a whole-island approach that integrates renewables with the blue economy to support economic diversification

Nearly 60% of SIDS’ population is under 30, making #youth the driving force of sustainable energy innovation in #SIDS. On the road to #COP29, we must work with them to create environments that empower their leadership, ensuring the convergence of all efforts toward enabling SIDS to proactively define their energy-for-development pathways. ☀️🌊🏝️

#EnergyForDevelopment ⚡️#RisingUpForSIDS

posts.caption:

It calls for urgent action to mobilize finance at scale to ensure affordable, reliable, and sustainable energy for all, alongside investments in resilient cross-border energy infrastructure.

Unlocking the scale of private investment in clean energy will require policy de-risking mechanisms to enhance the financial viability of renewable projects, incentivizing private capital, affordable tariffs, and expanded energy services. Given that 40% of low- and middle-income countries are facing severe debt issues, targeted financial flows and equitable redistribution are essential for accelerating renewable energy deployment in the Global South.

posts.title: India’s unique energy transition highlights how a nation can balance growing energy demand with the need for reliable access
posts.caption:
India’s unique energy transition highlights how a nation can balance growing energy demand with the need for reliable access and sustainability. Since 2000, half a billion people have gained access to electricity, and India has become the 4th largest renewable energy producer globally.

I am pleased to have joined a great session during the #SDG7 Action Forum, with Jessica Seddon, Soumya Swaminathan  Rishika Das Roy  William Brent  Abhishek Jain, and Arunabha Ghosh  highlighting India’s energy transition and the important lessons that can guide other nations in their own energy journeys. 💡

Disruptive approaches are needed to accelerate a just energy transition:

1. Leverage an integrated approach of policy, market development and digital innovation 
2. Integrated energy governance - engaging communities in decision making processes and support gender responsive policies
3. Develop strong policy reforms for transformative changes such as fossil fuel subsidies reforms to renewables and e-mobility

How can we learn from other countries' transition pathways and tailor these approaches to our interventions? 💡

At UNDP, we draw on India’s experience to support nations globally, particularly in Africa, helping advance decentralized energy solutions and enable a just transition for coal-dependent regions.

#EnergyForDevelopment

posts.caption:
During the #SDG7 Action Forum, I had the honor of opening a session on clean cooking alongside partners from the The World Bank  World Health Organization, Sustainable Energy for All (SEforALL)   and @UNDESA.

I emphasized four critical actions we must take to ensure we don't lose momentum on clean cooking.

•⁠  ⁠First, integrate clean cooking into energy transition, climate, and development policies, ensuring alignment with electrification and national goals.
•⁠  ⁠Second, strengthen finance access through capacity building, innovation, and private sector collaboration.
•⁠  ⁠⁠Third, tailor solutions to local needs and promote job creation by understanding consumer behaviors
•⁠  ⁠⁠Fourth, leverage data insights and blended finance models to de-risk investments, making clean cooking more attractive to investors.

By focusing on these actions, we can achieve tangible progress on clean cooking & drive the global shift towards a just and inclusive energy transition.

#EnergyForDevelopment #UNGA

1.⁠ ⁠Mobilize investment in energy efficiency across buildings, industry, and transport, including achieving 10,000 MW of energy savings by 2030 through energy efficiency measures
2.⁠ ⁠Advance renewable energy initiatives in line with Iran’s target of 30,000 MW by 2030, with a focus on electrification in big cities like Tehran through electric vehicles (EVs)

In my opening remarks, I emphasized three key points: the transformative convergence of the data revolution with renewable energy, the imperative of embedding innovation into the very fabric of our sustainable energy systems, and the advancement of inclusive technologies to bridge innovation gaps. ⚡️

posts.title: As COP16 Colombia on biodiversity begins, we have an opportunity to show how renewable energy can support both climate action
posts.caption:
As COP16 Colombia  on biodiversity begins, we have an opportunity to show how renewable energy can support both climate action and biodiversity conservation.

Scaling up renewable energy is imperative for mitigating climate change, and with careful planning, it can enhance biodiversity protection. By deploying renewable solutions like wind, solar, and photovoltaics that incorporate biomimicry—mimicking natural processes such as the efficiency of photosynthesis—we can create energy nature-based solutions that harmonize with local habitats, solving electricity access challenges while safeguarding ecosystems. 🌱

Through strategic environmental assessments, renewable energy projects can do more than just power communities—they can reduce carbon emissions, protect habitats, and minimize disruption to fragile ecosystems. posts.caption:
60% of electricity in Latin America and the Caribbean is already generated from #renewables, double the global average. With abundant hydropower, solar PV, and wind potential, along with 60% of the world’s lithium reserves essential for battery technology, the region has the capacity to leverage this transition to redefine sustainable development while securing local benefits for its communities. 

Moreover, this shift also promises employment opportunities, with #energy sector jobs projected to increase by over 15% by 2030, particularly in clean energy technologies and in the critical mineral sector. This momentum positions LAC to aim even higher by 2030, and even more ambitious goals than currently set in national targets can be made possible through strengthened cooperation, financial mobilization, innovative policy, and digital advancements, which will be essential building blocks for what could be a “second generation of the energy transition.” 

This approach can extend beyond energy production to include key areas like transport electrification and sustainable mining, positioning LAC as a global blueprint for just energy transitions at scale. With COP16 and the Latin American Energy Organization (OLADE) Energy Week now underway, LAC can maintain and accelerate their momentum toward a sustainable, resilient future powered by clean energy.

posts.caption:
One year ago, at COP28 UAE  we set the ambitious target of tripling renewable energy capacity and doubling energy efficiency by 2030. Today, at COP29 Azerbaijan  the urgency to shift from ambition to action is evident.
On the sidelines of #COP29, I joined a key discussion on how to unlock Africa’s energy potential to drive sustainable development, a session co-organized by UNDP  and the Italian Presidency of the #G7. 🫱🏽‍🫲🏼

Three key catalysts emerged:
1.	Streamline policy regulations and provide technical assistance to advance more projects to financial closure, building a pipeline of scalable, bankable projects.
2.	Innovative guarantee schemes to address financial barriers by providing a safety net to investors and lenders, encouraging investment by reducing perceived risks.
3.	 Leverage #digital to optimize energy systems, reduce costs, and attract private investment by increasing data availability, and the scalability and resilience of renewables infrastructure.

We spotlighted the” Energy for Growth in Africa” initiative—a strategic partnership between UNDP, the Italian Government, and the #G7—aimed at catalyzing Africa’s clean energy transformation through strategic investment, policy support, and multi-stakeholder collaboration. In synergy with initiatives like Mission 300, together, we can mobilize public, private, and development finance to unlock the full potential of Africa’s clean energy revolution.

posts.caption:
🌊 SIDS have consistently shown resilience and leadership in protecting their unique cultural and geographic heritage through bold commitments and strong political will, including pledges by many to achieve 100% renewable electricity by 2030.

At @COP29 in Azerbaijan, @UNDP and @AOSIS joined forces to host a session that provided a platform for discussing and positioning actionable opportunities to operationalize the priorities of the ABAS declaration, focusing on how to accelerate a just energy transition to unlock development opportunities in SIDS.

Key action steps to advance the energy-for-development pathway in SIDS: 

1. Advance a just energy transition to unlock transformative development across key sectors such as e-mobility, sustainable tourism, urban agriculture, and fisheries – tailored to the needs of each island community. 🏝️🚌
2. Leverage digital innovation to transition from traditional centralized systems to smart grids and digital platforms that optimize local electricity networks, enhancing resilience and efficiency, particularly in regions prone to natural disasters. 🌱
3. Scale financial mechanisms like debt-for-nature & energy swaps, blended finance funds, and National Laboratories of Financial Innovation to mobilize the capital needed to reach the $5.9 USD billion annually to meet their renewable energy target by 2030.  💡

@UNDP, in partnership with @AOSIS, has introduced a strategic approach addressing the ABAS declaration, detailed in our policy brief, “Advancing a Just Energy Transition in SIDS.” Presented during the event, this paper outlines key sustainable energy opportunities for the next decade of development in SIDS, to drive equitable economic growth and enhance resilience for integrated human development. ⚡️

1. Robust de-risking mechanisms that reduce financial risk and attract private capital to clean energy projects.
2. Innovative finance instruments like blended finance and thematic bonds to mobilize large-scale investments and address market inefficiencies.
3. Strategic use of #digital to enhance investment allocation and ensure data-driven decision-making.

UNDP is a leader on supporting countries to access, channel, and deliver finance towards energy & climate goals. Our collective ambitions to #3xRenewables is critical to keep 1.5°C within reach. However, current NDCs cover only 12% of this target, and with the next round of NDCs due in 2025, this offers an opportunity to place advancing an energy transition as a priority for NDCs. ☀️

On the session “Pathways to Energy Integration in NDCs,” co-hosted by @‌IRENA and @Ocean Conservancy, I highlighted three key opportunities to make NDCs ambitious and actionable, focusing on scaling sustainable renewable energy:

1. Support countries in creating bankable energy projects integrated with their NDCs, ensuring these plans are actionable and backed by comprehensive sectoral investment analyses.
2. ⁠Promote financial innovation & implement tools like credit guarantees and blended finance, facilitating debt-smart energy transition financing in developing countries.
3. ⁠Leverage digital technologies to help identify optimal investment opportunities, ensure optimized off-grid solutions & enable data-driven policymaking.

UNDP  and United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF)  are supporting these efforts by scaling up capital for renewable energy and developing innovative guarantee schemes that provide safety nets for investors and lenders, reducing perceived risks to move renewable energy projects from pipeline to financial closure.

posts.title: As #COP16 begins in Riyadh, the world faces an urgent challenge: 40% of global land is degraded, costing over 10% of annual G
posts.caption:
As #COP16 begins in Riyadh, the world faces an urgent challenge: 40% of global land is degraded, costing over 10% of annual GDP and threatening livelihoods for billions. Renewable energy holds the potential to drive solutions—powering irrigation systems, enhancing water security, and restoring degraded ecosystems. 🌱

To realize this potential, scaling energy finance is essential to mobilize the investments needed for sustainable development and resilience for the 2.6 billion people directly impacted by land degradation.

posts.title: Desertification affects 52% of agricultural land, costing 10% of global GDP and threatening food and water security for over
posts.caption:
Desertification affects 52% of agricultural land, costing 10% of global GDP and threatening food and water security for over 2.6 billion people. This demands urgent, transformative investments in integrated solutions across the water-energy-food nexus.

At COP16, I had the privilege of moderating a session co-hosted by UNDP, UNCDF, ICC Saudi Arabia, and Desert Technologies, where leaders from the financial sector, private sector, and public sector explored a key question: How can we catalyze investments in sustainable energy for land and water management to build resilience and unlock development opportunities?

💡 Key Takeaways:

1️⃣ Financial Institutions: Innovative mechanisms such as blended finance, green bonds, and guarantees are essential to de-risk investments, mobilize capital, and scale solutions in high-risk regions.

2️⃣ Private Sector: The private sector plays a pivotal role in developing bankable renewable energy projects, mitigating risks, and fostering sustainable growth.

3️⃣ Media as a Catalyst: By amplifying success stories, media bridges gaps between stakeholders and beneficiaries, driving collective action and highlighting community resilience.

Partnerships among financial institutions, sovereign wealth funds like Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, and international organizations are vital. These multi-sector collaborations are key to combating desertification, restoring ecosystems, and ensuring resilient livelihoods. 🌱

Our conversations at COP16 reaffirmed this: Innovative energy finance is not just an imperative—it’s an opportunity for a resilient future.

#COP16Riyadh #OurLandOurFuture #EnergyTransition #EnergyForDevelopment⚡️

posts.title: For the first time in 15 years, we have a new climate finance goal — but is it enough, and more importantly, does it respond
posts.caption:
For the first time in 15 years, we have a new climate finance goal — but is it enough, and more importantly, does it respond to the ambitions of the UAE consensus on clean energy adopted in COP28?  🌎
 
As we close out 2024 and reflect on progress made and the work still ahead, we are sharing this special edition bulletin on financing the sustainable energy revolution 👉  https://lnkd.in/eRFEfQdq
 
The New Collective Quantified Goal adopted at COP29 committed $300 billion per year by 2035, which marks a step forward in mobilizing resources. However, developing nations need annual investment to rise from $770 billion in 2022 to $2.2–2.8 trillion by the early 2030s.
Delivering the COP28 commitments on tripling renewables and doubling energy efficiency depends on bold reforms and collaborative innovation to close the energy finance gap and achieve a just energy transition. 💡
 
Beyond mobilizing private capital and creating a strong enabling environment through policy de-risking to scaling the quantity, focus must shift to the quality and impact of financing. Resources need to be accessible, strategically allocated, and equitably distributed to the regions and populations that need them most. Innovations in digital technologies, data, and AI also play a key role, reducing costs, optimizing resources, and de-risking investments. 📈
 
Happy holidays to our entire sustainable energy family! ⚡️
 
Here’s to continuing our efforts together for a just and impactful energy transition in the year to come. 
 
#EnergyRevolution #EnergyForDevelopment ⚡️#GlobalFinance #EnergyTransition

posts.caption:
I was pleased to participate to a round table in the role of youth in the just energy transition during #IRENA 15a. The energy transition is set to create 50 million new jobs by 2050—jobs that today’s youth will inherit. But young people aren’t just the leaders of tomorrow—they’re already driving change today. At the closing high level panel of the IRENA Youth Forum, we saw firsthand how youth are leading innovation and advancing clean energy solutions across the globe. 

To scale this impact, we need more than isolated efforts—we need inclusive, action-driven approaches that prioritize youth-led initiatives. By 2030, investments in the Global South need to triple to meet growing energy demands, and youth must be central to these transformations. 

Initiatives like #Youth4Climate, Green Growth and Jobs Accelerator Programme are designed to provide young people with the tools, training, and networks they need to lead in a just energy transitions. 

Youth is not a phase; they are leading up to the sustainable energy revolution. It’s time to turn pledges into action and ensure youth are at the forefront of this global transformation. Let’s act now for real, lasting change. #IRENA15A #EnergyforDevelopment #SustainableEnergyRevolution

posts.title: 2024 reminded us of the dual crises shaping our world—a record-breaking year for global temperatures and a pivotal year for r
posts.caption:
2024 reminded us of the dual crises shaping our world—a record-breaking year for global temperatures and a pivotal year for renewable energy progress. Clean energy investments surpassed $2 trillion, and renewables outpaced fossil fuels. Yet, these advancements remain unevenly distributed, with low- and middle-income countries capturing only 15% of global clean energy investments (excluding China). 

This stark inequity underscores an urgent opportunity: accelerating the energy transition to drive inclusive growth and decisive climate action. 

I had the privilege of participating in the 15th IRENA Assembly on Innovative Renewables Risk Mitigation Instruments, where key stakeholders convened to explore solutions for scaling investments in underserved markets.  

💡 Key Takeaways from the Assembly: 
 
1️⃣ Lowering Financing Costs: High interest rates disproportionately impact renewable projects. Complementing fiscal strategies with non-fiscal tools—such as guarantees and concessional funding—can attract investment in high-risk markets 
2️⃣ Smarter Risk Mitigation mechanism: Governments in developing countries need support through innovative tools like green bonds, debt-for-clean-energy swaps, and public-private partnerships, which de-risk investments and attract private capital. 
3️⃣ Harnessing Digital Innovations: The integration of geospatial analytics and AI, such as the Clean Energy Equity Index, ensures smarter, data-driven investment decisions that prioritize equity and efficiency. 

As we approach major milestones like COP30 in Brazil and the G20 under South Africa’s leadership, the urgency to mobilize capital, strengthen local systems, and foster strategic partnerships cannot be overstated. 

Together, let us drive a sustainable energy revolution that bridges gaps, unlocks opportunities, and accelerates the transition to clean energy for all. 

#IRENA15A #EnergyforDevelopment

posts.title: Antigua and Barbuda is leading the way in advancing a just energy transition. With 23% savings from reduced fossil fuel impor
posts.caption:
Antigua and Barbuda is leading the way in advancing a just energy transition. With 23% savings from reduced fossil fuel imports—equivalent to approximately $60 million annually—and an ambitious target of achieving 100% renewable energy by 2030, the country is poised to deliver transformative benefits for its people and the planet.

I had the privilege of meeting H.E. Minister of Energy, Hon. Melford Nicholas, to discuss implementing the ABAS principles. Our discussions focused on key strategies to accelerate this transition while promoting inclusive growth and climate resilience:

1️⃣ Innovative Financial Mechanisms: Exploring options such as guarantee schemes and concessional loans to attract international investment. Collaborations between UNDP and United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF)  aim to maximize these opportunities.

2️⃣ Digitalization for Energy Transition: Utilizing digital technologies to enhance renewable energy integration and enable e-mobility solutions.

3️⃣ Innovative Energy Storage Solutions: Implementing advanced storage systems to manage peak demand and stabilize the grid.

Antigua and Barbuda is a shining example of leadership in sustainable development and climate action. UNDP  is at the forefront to support this journey toward a sustainable energy revolution. 💡✨

posts.title: To meet SDG7 targets by 2030, we need to provide electricity to 157 million more people and clean cooking solutions to 334 mi
posts.caption:
To meet SDG7 targets by 2030, we need to provide electricity to 157 million more people and clean cooking solutions to 334 million annually. This requires $3 to $4.5 trillion in annual investments—not just to close gaps but as an opportunity to drive inclusive growth, create jobs, and improve lives. 

At the 15th IRENA Assembly, I had the honor of delivering opening remarks on Sustainable Energy: The Road Ahead. With global energy demand rising as the population grows by 25%, we have a unique opportunity to lift 1.18 billion people out of energy poverty while accelerating a cleaner, more sustainable future. 

Actions for a Sustainable Energy Revolution

1. Scale up financing: Mobilize $3–4.5 trillion annually, shift investments to the Global South, and eliminate market inefficiencies and regulatory barriers. 

2. Innovative finance in the Global South: Support initiatives like Mission 300, Energy for Growth, and the Africa Minigrids Program to expand energy access, accelerate the transition, and create opportunities for inclusive growth. 

3. Leverage digital, data, and AI: Geospatial tools like the UNDP-IBM Clean Energy Equity Index can identify investment opportunities, optimize energy systems, and ensure an equitable energy transition. 

The energy transition is a powerful opportunity to create a brighter, more inclusive future. Together, let’s champion a sustainable energy revolution that benefits everyone, everywhere. 

#IRENA15A #SDG7 #EnergyforDevelopment.

posts.title: In 2022, developed countries mobilized $115.9 billion for climate finance, but the efficiency of these investments is declini
posts.caption:
In 2022, developed countries mobilized $115.9 billion for climate finance, but the efficiency of these investments is declining. Private co-financing per public dollar fell to just 24 cents, down from 51 cents in 2013. 

How can we make every dollar work smarter to catalyze systemic change? 

On the first day of the 15th IRENA Assembly, it was a pleasure to speak at the Ministerial Roundtable on Scaling Up Finance to Support the Energy Transition in Emerging Markets and Developing Economies. 

To address the financing gap, we must act decisively: 

1- Lower the cost of capital for clean energy in EMDEs through de-risking mechanisms, blended finance, and performance-based instruments. 

2- Streamline international support by creating strategic alliances and deepening collaboration for bankable projects, unlocking a $65 billion investment opportunity to connect 265 million people to clean energy. 

3- Leverage tryptic of digital data and AI to optimize investment decisions, accelerating renewable projects and ensuring equitable energy access for local communities. 

Together, through smarter and more impactful investments, we can bridge the financing gap and drive an inclusive, sustainable energy transformation. 

#IRENA15A #EnergyforDevelopment #SustainableEnergyRevolution

posts.title: SIDS face a unique energy challenge: 90% fossil fuel reliance, 3x higher electricity costs, and extreme climate vulnerability
posts.caption:
SIDS face a unique energy challenge: 90% fossil fuel reliance, 3x higher electricity costs, and extreme climate vulnerability. But renewable energy offers a pathway to self-reliance, climate resilience, and economic growth. 🌱⚡ 

To unlock this potential, international partners should focus on 3 areas: 

1️⃣ Innovative Financing: #SIDS 🏝️ need $5.9B annually for renewable energy. With debt-for-energy swaps and blended finance, SIDS can save $3.3B annually in reduced fossil fuel imports. 

2️⃣ Capacity Building & SIDS-SIDS Cooperation: Knowledge exchanges and regional partnerships, like floating solar, help integrate renewables at scale. 

3️⃣ Digital Transformation: AI, IoT, and data analytics enable smarter energy systems. Initiatives like CloudSolar in Barbados democratize solar access and empower local investments. 

Guided by the #Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS, we must drive ‘disruptive innovation’ and take collective action to turn a sustainable, equitable energy future into reality—one that meets today’s needs and enables future generations to build the future they envision. 🌍💡

posts.title: Today, at the margins of the Fifteenth Session of the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) Assembly and the World Fu
posts.caption:
Today, at the margins of the Fifteenth Session of the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA)  Assembly and the World Future Energy Summit, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF)  had hosted a vital side event on a Multi-stakeholder Innovative Energy Finance to Accelerate the Energy Transition in Developing Countries, and I had the privilege of moderating a disruptive and insightful discussion that brought together intergovernmental representatives, development partners, and private sector experts to explore key solutions to unlock the capital needed to accelerate the energy transition in developing countries. 

Here are three critical takeaways from today’s session: 

- Innovative Financing Mechanisms Are Key to Scaling Up: To close the $2.8 trillion investment gap for clean energy in developing countries, we must scale up blended finance, green bonds, and debt-for-energy swaps, complemented by nation-led energy strategies to ensure alignment with local needs and priorities. 

- Strengthening South-South Collaboration: The energy transition requires inclusive, cross-border collaboration, with initiatives like Mission 300, Africa Minigrid Program, and ETAF playing a crucial role in unlocking finance for high-risk markets, particularly in Africa and SIDS, where urgent energy access is needed. 

- Leveraging Digital and Data Technologies to Transform the Energy Landscape: Digital tools like AI and data analytics are transforming energy finance, enabling smarter decision-making, reducing risks, and optimizing energy systems to integrate renewables and improve efficiency while ensuring equity and sustainability. 

This discussion reminded us that closing the financing gap requires collaboration, innovation, and data-driven strategies to ensure an inclusive and equitable sustainable energy revolution. I would like to thank all our distinguished panelists for their continued dedication to ensure just energy transition. 

#EnergyforDevelopment #SustainableEnergyRevolution

posts.title: Achieving Africa’s energy and climate goals by 2030 requires over USD 200 billion in annual investments. To achieve this, we
posts.caption:
Achieving Africa’s energy and climate goals by 2030 requires over USD 200 billion in annual investments. To achieve this, we must implement clear strategies and secure increased international financial and technical support. 

I had the pleasure of meeting with Power Africa’s Cullen Hughes, Deputy Coordinator, and Carolyn Laurenzano, Development Partnerships Officer, to discuss how we can accelerate a just and equitable energy transition across the continent. Here are the key actions for progress:

1. Developing Pipeline of Bankable Projects: Initiatives like Mission 300, which aims to connect 300 million people in Sub-Saharan Africa to electricity by 2030, and the Africa Minigrids Program, a $65 billion opportunity, are critical for bridging financing gaps. 

2. Integrated Approach to Energy Transition: Unreliable power impacts life-saving services—half of Sub-Saharan Africa’s health facilities lack reliable electricity. Through Power Africa’s the Health Electrification and Telecommunications Alliance (HETA) and UNDP's Solar for Health, we are integrating energy and health to advance universal health coverage. 

3. Innovative Financing for Off-Grid Solutions: Over 60 million people in Africa already access electricity through off-grid solutions. To accelerate energy access, we need innovative financial models and business mechanisms to scale renewable off-grid energy. 

This is a call for urgent, collective action. Together, we can drive unprecedented progress in Africa through sustainable energy transformation. 

#EnergyforDevelopment #SustainableEnergyRevolution

posts.caption:
Advancing a Just Energy Transition in SIDS⚡️

The Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS outlined a clear priority for placing sustainable energy at the center of development - with many SIDS already leading the way towards 100% renewable energy in their power mix by 2030.  

This transition not only reaffirms their commitment to sustainability, but also presents a significant economic opportunity: while collectively adding 13 GW of new capacity, SIDS could save $3.3 billion annually (equivalent to 3.3% of GDP) by transitioning to 100% renewable energy.

For SIDS the transition to renewable energy serves as a powerful catalyst for integrated development solutions, enabling:
✅ Self-dependence
✅ Climate resilience
✅ Food security
✅ Economic diversification
✅ Sustainable development

posts.caption:
World Energy Day: Ensuring Access to Sustainable Energy for All 🔋💡

With today, as World Energy Day, marked as a time to reflect on “energy efficiency and production alternatives”, it is also important to consider how we, as a global community, recognize the value and importance of sustainable energy.

The COP28 UAE Consensus to Triple Renewable capacity and Double Efficiency by 2030 sets out a clear agenda. Yet at the core of these developments are communities and people — those who still lack their fundamental right to sustainable energy.⚡️

Today, nearly:

➡️ 1.18 billion people live in energy poverty.

➡️ 685 million people live without electricity access.

➡️ 2.1 billion people lacking access to fundamental clean cooking facilities.

➡️ 2 billion people live in conflict-affected areas where energy security is critical.

➡️ Nearly 1 billion people in the Global South lack electricity in healthcare facilities.

As countries update their NDCs for COP30, and the G20 presidency seeks to mobilize finance for a just energy transition, 2025 presents a critical opportunity to move from intent to impactful action.
 
We need to ensure that resources are accessible, strategically allocated, and equitably distributed to those who need them most. Sustainable energy is not only a component of the SDG7 Agenda —“Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all” — it is also a key enabler of the entire 2030 Agenda. 🌐

To out why, on this World Energy Day 2025, we must recognize the value and importance of a sustainable energy revolution, I invite you to read this latest edition of the Sustainable Energy Bulletin: 👉 bit.ly/411usOI

posts.title: Solid-State Batteries and The Future of Mobility 🔋🚀 As we move towards a more sustainable energy future, Solid-State Batterie
posts.caption:
Solid-State Batteries and The Future of Mobility 🔋🚀

As we move towards a more sustainable energy future, Solid-State Batteries (SSBs) are set to transform electric vehicles; renewable energy storage; and public transport. Unlike traditional lithium-ion batteries, SSBs use a solid electrolyte as opposed to a liquid one, offering higher energy density, improved safety, and longer lifecycle.🔋

But why Solid-State Batteries?

➡️ Higher Energy Density: Delivering 5X more energy for the same weight as conventional batteries, making them ideal for industrial applications.

➡️ Faster Charging Times: Fully charged in 10-15 minutes, unlike lithium-ion batteries.

➡️ Safer and More Stable: Addressing fire and safety concerns by using non-flammable solid materials.

➡️ 30-40% Weight Reduction: Improving the overall efficiency of the devices or vehicles they power.

➡️ 10-100 Hours of Energy Storage: Important for improving grid security and building resilient infrastructures for developing countries.

➡️ Lower Carbon Footprint: Using far fewer critical minerals like cobalt & nickel, reducing their overall climate impact by up to 39%.

Find out why, with the right investments and continued innovation, a future powered by clean and renewable energy is within reach in my latest interview with Arval Mobility Observatory: 👉 https://rb.gy/7vrjft

posts.caption:
Today, on International Women’s Day, we are reminded of the promises world leaders made 30 years ago in Beijing to deliver rights, equality and empowerment #ForAllWomenAndGirls
 
A key part of realizing these promises is ensuring a just and equitable energy transition. Sustainable energy and gender equality are deeply intertwined, yet key challenges persist in advancing both:
 
➡️ Energy poverty goes beyond being an infrastructure issue - it is a gendered crisis. On average, women and girls in Africa spend 50 hours a week collecting firewood, water and cooking – time that could be spent on education, improving livelihoods and health.🌐
 
➡️ Women are more than energy consumers – they are agents of change as energy producers, innovators and decision makers. 🙏
 
While the benefits of an inclusive and diverse workforce are clear, the gender divide in the energy sector persists. Women make up only 20% of the energy workforce, despite making up 40% of workers globally. Women-led startups receive less than 3% of energy investment capital.
 
Investing in women-led initiatives and empowering women as leaders in the energy sector can drive solutions for the just transition. ⚡️
 
2025 is a critical year for the gender-energy nexus. Milestones including CSW69 and COP30 present key moments for accelerated action. While #SDG7 is one of only six SDGs without gender-specific indicators, this should be no excuse not to scale up action towards achieving a gender-responsive just transition!
 
Now is the time to invest in women-led energy initiatives, advocate for gender-responsive energy policies, and support women’s leadership in the energy sector.

Not just on #IWD, but every day.
 
#SustainableEnergy #GenderEquality #IWD2025 #CSW69

posts.title: How do we solve the energy access paradox? ⚡ This week, leaders at the 2025 Sustainable Energy for All Global Forum tackle th
posts.caption:
How do we solve the energy access paradox? ⚡  
 
This week, leaders at the 2025 Sustainable Energy for All Global Forum tackle this pressing question.  
 
Over 658 million people still lack electricity — 571 million in Sub-Saharan Africa alone. The regional divide is growing. Yet sustainable energy is more than a commodity; it’s key to realizing development and human rights by powering education, health, livelihoods, food and water security and more.  
 
The opportunities are clear. Universal energy access in Sub-Saharan Africa could create 4 million jobs by 2030, while technological advances make sustainable electricity the most cost-effective solution. In a time of growing geopolitical tensions, sustainable energy offers a pathway to energy independence. 
 
We know the solutions. Closing the gap by 2030 requires $30 billion annually, with half of the investments needed in Sub-Saharan Africa. Driving large-scale electrification requires unlocking technological solutions and focusing on de-risking policy and finance to attract private capital. 
 
The world cannot afford to leave 658 million people in the dark. 
 
💡 Our latest Sustainable Energy Bulletin explores the path to bridging the gap, latest trends, and key opportunities ahead 👉 https://bit.ly/4bKL5Dj

posts.title: Achieving Mission 300 requires a fundamental shift in how we approach Energy Access!⚡️ Yesterday, in a timely and critical se
posts.caption:
Achieving Mission 300 requires a fundamental shift in how we approach Energy Access!⚡️ 

Yesterday, in a timely and critical session organized by The World Bank  and ESMAP - Energy Sector Management Assistance Program  - Energy Sector Management Assistance Program at the #SEforALLForum in Barbados, we discussed what it will take to scale distributed renewable energy and unlock financing to reach 300 million people by 2030: 

1️⃣ Distributed renewables must be embedded in national energy strategies: Clear interconnection policies are critical to ensuring mini-grids can complement, rather than compete with, national grids. When integrated effectively, they could provide up to 11% of new electricity connections. 

2️⃣ The cost of capital is a barrier to scaling clean energy: High borrowing costs and debt burdens are locking out investment. Policy and financial de-risking mechanisms, including debt-for-energyswaps and financial instruments, must be expanded. 

3️⃣ A whole-of-society approach is essential: Civil society, local leadership, and communities must be at the center of designing and scaling energy solutions, as seen in Guinea’s successful decentralized projects. 

Technology alone will not deliver M300. Policy and regulatory reforms, coupled with strategic financing, are needed to turn solutions into large-scale impact.🌐

UNDP  and United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF)  are connecting policy, finance, and innovation to drive transformation. We are moving beyond business-as-usual approaches and rethinking financing clean energy to drive meaningful and lasting development impact. 

Through initiatives like the Africa Minigrids Program, Solar for Health, and financial de-risking instruments, we are committed to scale clean energy through collaboration!🤝⚡️
#EnergyForDevelopment #SEforALLForum #SustainableFinance #EnergyTransition

posts.title: Powering the SDGs: From Connections to Consumption.💡 By 2050, the global population will grow by nearly 2 billion, driving el
posts.caption:
Powering the SDGs: From Connections to Consumption.💡

By 2050, the global population will grow by nearly 2 billion, driving electricity demand up by nearly 50%. While clean energy generation is on track to break new records over the 2025-2027 forecast period (with renewable capacity projected to triple by 2030) a critical question remains: how do people access energy? 

Yesterday at the at the #SEforALLForum, we gathered with an excellent group of experts -  Sarah Malm  (Gogla), Cassady Walters  (Rockefeller Foundation/GEAPP), Alexander Obiechina  Ltd), and Martijn Veen  (SNV) - to explore this pressing concern and discuss how finance, decentralized solutions, and innovation can unlock an inclusive, affordable, and productive energy future. 

Achieving universal electrification by 2030 requires $52 billion per year: but finance alone isn’t the answer. To close this gap, we must: 

➡️ Shift our focus from generating energy, to delivering it to people affordably, efficiently and securely. 

➡️ Link decentralized renewable energy solutions with productive uses that unlock a pathway to inclusive growth and improved livelihoods, creating a spiral of positive development outcomes. 

➡️ Increase energy storage capacity to accommodate new variable, context specific, renewable energy generation. 

➡️ Revolutionize our energy supply by harnessing AI to optimize energy storage systems. 

While we have made significant progress in energy generation, we are reminded that technology alone will not get us to our goals. With 685 million people still living without electricity, our work is far from over.  

We need innovative financial models, inclusive business strategies, and above all else, a commitment to leaving no one behind!☀️🤝⚡️
#EnergyForDevelopment  #EnergyAccess #RenewableEnergy #SustainableDevelopment

posts.title: Today, I joined fellow experts and practitioners at the Think7 Summit panel on "Energy Security and Climate", hosted by the C
posts.caption:
Today, I joined fellow experts and practitioners at the Think7 Summit panel on "Energy Security and Climate", hosted by the Centre for International Governance Innovation (CIGI).
 
Climate change and energy security are deeply interlinked. While the global energy system fuels development, it also drives climate change, accounting for 75% of greenhouse gas emissions. As climate change intensifies, the links with energy security deepen. With conflicts, debt, and rising inequalities straining economies, the G7 has a strategic opportunity to support a just, inclusive energy transition that ensures no one is left behind:
 
➡️ Energy security is climate resilience. Despite record growth in renewables, climate disruptions in 2023 slashed wind energy output by up to 30% and hydropower by over 50% in some regions. Our energy systems must be designed for the climate of today - not the past.
 
➡️ Securing energy means rethinking how and where we invest. Over 90% of clean energy growth is in advanced economies and China, while SIDS face climate losses up to 9% of GDP and unsustainable debt. Through innovative tools like Debt Swaps for Energy, UNDP is helping unlock renewable investment - turning fiscal constraints into opportunities for resilience.
 
➡️ Digital, data, and AI are the new core of energy infrastructure. With electricity demand set to double by 2050, climate intelligence - from predictive models to smart grids - is essential to build resilient, investable, and future-ready energy systems.
 
Now is the time for the G7 to move from ambition to implementation. With 1.18 billion people still living in energy poverty, energy security must drive human development through partnerships, stronger Global South-North cooperation and targeted investment.
 
Thank you to CIGI and fellow panelists for a timely, forward-looking discussion.
 
#T7CIGI #T72025 #Think7CIGI #EnergyforDevelopment #EnergyTransition

posts.title: Electric utopia or elite privilege? Rethinking e-mobility for the Global South🚗⚡ The future of mobility is electric - but is
posts.caption:
Electric utopia or elite privilege? Rethinking e-mobility for the Global South🚗⚡
 
The future of mobility is electric - but is it truly global? In 2023, nearly one in five vehicles sold worldwide was electric, and by 2035 electric vehicles are projected to make up almost 50% of the global auto market. However, a staggering 95% of EV sales are concentrated in China, Europe, and the United States.
 
While the Global South remains largely on the sidelines, accounting for only a small fraction of these sales, the shift to e-mobility holds immense potential. It presents an opportunity to:
 
✅ Improve air quality and health outcomes, particularly in the Global South, where air pollution claims millions of lives, accounting for 89% of the 4.2 million premature deaths annually.
 
✅ Reduce reliance on imported fossil fuels, enhancing energy security and economic resilience.
 
✅ Electrify shared and public transport, ensuring affordable and inclusive mobility solutions, revitalizing a form of widely affordable transportation essential for last-mile connectivity.
 
✅ Create jobs and foster economic growth, as EV manufacturing alone is expected to create 1.5 million new jobs by 2030.
 
Despite solutions emerging, such as innovative financing models; digital technologies; and localized electrification strategies, the question remains: how can the Global South harness the e-mobility revolution to drive sustainable development and climate action?
 
I invite you all to explore these insights and the opportunities that lie ahead for the Global South to transition to e-mobility in my latest illuminem article: https://lnkd.in/dEQ62xiy

posts.caption:
Delighted to have joined colleagues from @UNDP Bhutan on their webinar co-organized by @Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources to explore Bhutan’s green hydrogen potential.
 
In 2023, the world produced 97 million tons of hydrogen - but less than 1% came from low-emission sources. The momentum is growing, but the challenge is clear: how we choose to develop green hydrogen, and for whom, will define whether it delivers on its promise:

1️⃣ Green hydrogen must be a tool for development - not just decarbonization. With youth unemployment at 28.6% and 55% of the population living in rural areas, Bhutan needs growth that is inclusive and job-rich. Green hydrogen could support this, if linked to skills development, rural infrastructure, and the broader vision of Gross National Happiness.

2️⃣ Sustainability is not one-size-fits-all. While Bhutan has vast hydropower resources, green hydrogen production raises concerns about water use, land access, and biodiversity. It takes 9 litres of water to produce 1 kg of hydrogen. In a mountainous country, with seasonal water stress, these trade-offs matter. The goal must be to balance ambition with realism, scale with sustainability.

3️⃣ The transition must be just and equitable. That means ensuring benefits reach everyone. We should avoid extractive investment models and prioritize policies that keep value local, empower communities, and protect natural and cultural heritage.
 
@UNDP remains committed to supporting Bhutan's green hydrogen journey: not as champions of a single solution, but as partners dedicated to inclusive long-term impact.
 
For Bhutan, a whole-of-society approach is key. A just energy transition is not only about technology - it’s about ensuring that the benefits of innovation reach everyone, with inclusion at its core. Watch here 👉🏾 https://lnkd.in/ej-_kr3H
 
Thank you to colleagues and fellow panelists for a timely, forward-looking discussion.

#EnergyForDevelopment #GreenHydrogen #JustTransition

posts.title: ⚡ Energy is a fundamental enabler of development — and nowhere is this more evident than in the health sector. It delivers on
posts.caption:
⚡ Energy is a fundamental enabler of development — and nowhere is this more evident than in the health sector. It delivers one of the highest returns in climate adaptation, yet remains critically underfunded.

🔌 1 in 4 health facilities globally lacks electricity, and at least 25,000 in sub-Saharan Africa operate with no electricity access. Bridging this gap requires four strategic shifts:

✅ Integrating Sustainable Energy into Health Policies and Planning
Nearly 1 billion people rely on health facilities without reliable electricity. Energy must be integrated into health strategies and Universal Health Coverage (UHC) planning.

✅ Financing Sustainable Energy for Health Resilience
An estimated $4.9 billion is needed to electrify facilities in 63 low- and middle-income countries. Funding should prioritize decentralized renewable energy as core health infrastructure.

✅ Promoting Data-driven Decisionmaking
In 46 low- and middle-income countries, 60% of health facilities face unreliable power. Energy audits, monitoring, geospatial data, and AI-powered storage can improve reliability.

✅ Prioritizing Sustainable Energy in Fragile and Crisis-affected Settings
With 2 billion people in conflict-affected areas, solar mini-grids and Pay-As-You-Go models ensure care continues when the grid fails.

Investing in sustainable energy is not just about powering facilities — it’s about powering health systems that save lives.

#EnergyforHealth #UNDP #WorldHealthDay

posts.title: Closing Africa’s Energy Access Gap: Looking Beyond the Traditional Grid to a Decentralized Future.🌍⚡️ The global energy acces
posts.caption:
Closing Africa’s Energy Access Gap: Looking Beyond the Traditional Grid to a Decentralized Future.🌍⚡️
 
The global energy access gap is widening, and it is increasingly a challenge for countries in Sub-Saharan Africa. Of the 685 million people globally without electricity, 571 million live in Sub-Saharan Africa.
 
Grid expansion alone will not close Africa’s energy access gap.
 
Decentralized Renewable Energy (DRE) solutions, such as solar mini-grids and off-grid systems, are already offering a fast and cost-effective path to electrification. Not only could they provide 80% of new electricity connections in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, but they have already provided electricity access to 560 million people worldwide. These solutions go beyond access - they have become a catalyst for change in Africa:
 
➡️ Nigeria’s market-driven approach has enabled the deployment of +100 solar-powered mini-grids.
 
➡️ Easy Solar has brought power to +1M people in Sierra Leone and Liberia since 2016.
 
➡️ Retrofitting diesel-powered irrigation system with solar energy helped mango farmers boost yields by 185% per tree in Tanzania.
 
But to be successful, governments must be proactive in planning regulatory frameworks that enable mini-grids to complement national grids rather than compete with them; as without clear interconnection policies, these projects risk becoming stranded assets. Through leveraging digitalization, AI, and advanced grid technologies, smart decentralized systems can enhance efficiency, minimize energy losses and optimize renewable energy integration to power a sustainable and inclusive energy future.⚡️♻️
 
To find out why the future of energy in Africa lies beyond the traditional grid, I invite you to read this latest edition of the Sustainable Energy Bulletin here: 👉 https://bit.ly/4bKL5Dj

posts.title: This Earth Day 2025, we take time to reflect on the importance of the circular energy revolution. The transition to sustainab
posts.caption:
This Earth Day 2025, we take time to reflect on the importance of the circular energy revolution. The transition to sustainable energy is more important than ever: not only for the environment but for the global economy and society as a whole.
 
Historically, the production and consumption of energy has been responsible for >75% of greenhouse gas emissions - making it the primary driver of climate change and global warming. However, sustainable energy solutions, such solar and wind power, are becoming increasingly more accessible and cost-effective. In 2023, renewables accounted for 30% of global electricity supply. By 2030, electricity is projected to grow six times faster than energy demand driven by a surge in renewable energy adoption and the rise in electric vehicles. 
 
Yet as demand for electricity and battery storage & utilization increases, so too does the need for critical minerals. While less harmful than fossil fuels, we need to also ask ourselves:
 
➡️ With battery storage capacity currently at 3TWh, anticipated to triple by 2030, what will this mean for the battery sector on the whole? How and where will this impact on the demand for critical minerals?
 
 ➡️ Extracting minerals sustainably remains a challenge, with lithium production requiring 2.2 million liters of water per ton - an immense demand in regions with limited water access. How do we ensure that we are not exacerbating as opposed to enabling human development?
 
➡️ With 54% of critical mineral reserves sitting on Indigenous People’s land, how do we ensure these actors have a voice?
 
➡️ Although Africa currently holds over 50% of global reserves and production of cobalt and manganese, which are critical components for batteries, how do we ensure that these benefits are evenly distributed amongst all members of society? 
 
While renewable electricity continues to scale up - reshaping markets and accelerating innovation - we are reminded today on #EarthDay of the importance of proceeding with caution. A sustainable, circular energy revolution is critical to transforming lives and our global economies, reducing carbon emissions, improving air quality, and preserving our natural resources.
 
#EnergyForDevelopment #EarthDay #SustainableEnergy #RenewableEnergy #ClimateAction #GoGreen

posts.title: Delighted to have joined the opening panel of “Advancing a Just Energy Transition Through Multilateral Action”, hosted by New
posts.caption:
Delighted to have joined the opening panel of “Advancing a Just Energy Transition Through Multilateral Action”, hosted by New America  alongside Dr. Chola Milambo, Permanent Representative of Zambia to the United Nations, and moderated by Heela Rasool-Ayub.
 
At a time of rising tariffs, deepening debt burdens, and widening divides in global finance, we face a series of fundamental questions: who defines the energy transition, who benefits from it, and how do we deliver justice at scale?
 
Here are three key messages discussed:

1️⃣ A just energy transition is not a choice, it is a human right: Energy powers health, education, and livelihoods. Nearly 60% of healthcare facilities in 46 low- and middle-income countries face unreliable power. Access to energy is access to life-saving services.
 
2️⃣ Access is no longer just about electricity, it’s about security: Only 2% of global clean energy investment reaches Africa. We need systems that deliver fit-for-purpose finance, debt reform, and de-risking mechanisms that allow countries to drive transitions that advance social protection, gender equality, and local development.
 
3️⃣ Digital and energy systems must be inclusive: AI, data infrastructure, and clean tech depend on critical minerals from the Global South. Yet the value often flows elsewhere. We must build shared digital infrastructure, ensure technology transfer, and promote governance that keeps value local and communities strengthened.
 
At UNDP Sustainable Energy Hub  Energy Hub, we are committed to partnering with countries to deliver transitions that are inclusive, intelligent, and rooted in development priorities. From COP30 to the G20 to FfD4, the path forward must be country-led, digitally enabled, and development-aligned.
 
#EnergyForDevelopment #JustTransntion #AccessForAll

posts.title: Achieving universal electricity access by 2030 will cost USD 30 billion a year: But how do we get there? While renewable ener
posts.caption:
Achieving universal electricity access by 2030 will cost USD 30 billion a year: But how do we get there?
 
While renewable energy investment in Africa grew 96% annually between 2010–2020 - outpacing global trends - the region still received just 2% of global renewable investment over two decades, with over 90% concentrated in a handful of countries. 
 
To close the energy access gap, it is estimated that Africa will require USD 25 billion annually. But public finance alone will not close the gap. Unlocking Africa’s energy future will require:
 ➡️ Deep sectoral reforms — with 58% of African utilities failing to recover operational costs, many remain financially unviable.
 ➡️ Cost-reflective tariffs and revenue certainty — essential to creating a stable investment climate.
 ➡️ Policy reforms — to allow private electricity providers to compete with state-run utilities.
 ➡️ Blended finance models — combining concessional capital with policy reform to de-risk and mobilize private investment at scale.
 
📌 Rwanda’s SEAP program is a strong example: backed by concessional loans, it extended 8,000+ km of power lines, connected 317,000+ new households, and trained 4,000 people — 30% of them women.
 
With the right policies, incentives, and blended finance, sustainable energy access in Africa is possible. The time to act is now - the world cannot afford to leave 685 million people in the dark. 💡

posts.title: Recent trends such as AI-generated Studio Ghibli images and AI Doll action figures allow users to “cartoonize” their lives. H
posts.caption:
Recent trends such as AI-generated Studio Ghibli images and AI Doll action figures allow users to “cartoonize” their lives. However, these requests impose significant strain on data centres, often leading to infrastructure malfunctions caused by overheating or “melting” due to high demand.

Since OpenAI launched its extended image rendering capabilities in April 2025, over 700 million image generation requests have been made. Unlike “typical” ChatGPT text requests, which consume 2.9Wh, these image requests reportedly consume 3.25Wh. The additional 0.35Wh energy consumption has amounted to over 245 MWh - equivalent to the energy used to power 2,800 10W LED bulbs for a year.

Yet, while servers work overtime to render these trends, 1.18 billion people still live in energy poverty, lacking access to air conditioning, heating, and lighting. This raises a critical question: While AI-generated images are increasing energy demand, how are digital technologies being used to close the access gap for those 1.18 billion energy-poor individuals?

Adopting digital technologies across the energy value chain can accelerate and economize the energy transition through:   
 
➡️ Enhancing efficiency and expanding access to renewable energy sources 
 
➡️ Identifying optimal investment opportunities and enabling informed based decision-making 
 
➡️ “Leapfrogging” traditional energy systems models by integrating more efficient and cost-effective energy solutions  

To learn more about how digital technologies are bridging this energy access divide, I invite you to read this previous edition of the Sustainable Energy Bulletin on Digital, Data, and AI here: 👉 https://lnkd.in/ey4__kbt     #EnergyForDevelopment #AI #EnergyAccess

posts.title: Grateful to have joined the panel on “Solutions for Clean Cooking to Advance the SDG Agenda”, co-hosted with the Council of E
posts.caption:
Grateful to have joined the panel on “Solutions for Clean Cooking to Advance the SDG Agenda”, co-hosted with the Council of Engineers for the Energy Transition (CEET). It was an important space to reaffirm what many of us in sustainable energy for development know well: clean cooking is not a side issue – it is a core pillar of a just and inclusive energy transition. 

Despite major gains in electrification and renewables, 2.1 billion people still rely on firewood, charcoal or dung to cook their meals. This is more than a technical challenge. It is a crisis of equity, health, gender justice, economic productivity and environmental sustainability. 

From the discussion, I emphasized three key action opportunities for scaling clean cooking access within sustainable energy systems: 

🔹 Integrate clean cooking into national electrification and energy access planning from the start. Clean cooking must be positioned as a core energy service – alongside lighting, refrigeration and productive uses – from the outset. This requires incorporating cooking energy demand into load forecasts, tariff design, appliance programmes, and rural mini-grid planning. When planning reflects the full needs of households, including cooking, the developmental impacts are significantly amplified. 

🔹 Scale blended finance and market-building instruments to unlock local market development. Despite offering an estimated $2.4 trillion in annual cost savings, clean cooking continues to receive < 1% of global energy investments. This imbalance reflects a broader failure to recognize clean cooking as a viable market. We must shift this narrative and mobilize coordinated public-private investment strategies. 

🔹 Leverage AI, geospatial tools, and smart technologies to enhance access, affordability, and targeting. The same technologies reshaping electricity access can revolutionize clean cooking. Digitalization offers a powerful opportunity to make clean cooking delivery more efficient, demand-responsive and inclusive. 

At UNDP’s Sustainable Energy Hub, we are supporting more than 80 projects across all regions, advancing clean cooking through technology, policy, and local enterprise development. The solutions exist. The time to act is now. 

To learn more about why clean cooking matters, what’s changing, and how we can scale solutions across the energy transition, I invite you to subscribe to the Sustainable Energy Hub’s bulletin: 👉 https://lnkd.in/eJGZ7XXq 

#EnergyForDevelopment #CleanCooking #SDG3 #SDG5 #SDG7 #SDG8 #SDG13

posts.title: Clean cooking needs $8 billion a year to reach universal access – but we’re mobilizing barely a third of that. This isn’t jus
posts.caption:
Clean cooking needs $8 billion a year to reach universal access – but we’re mobilizing barely a third of that. This isn’t just a funding gap. It’s a development failure.  

As I said early today: “We’re paying trillions of dollars to avoid spending billions." 

At what point do we stop calling this an “investment gap” when the cost of doing nothing is a thousand times higher? 

The numbers speak for themselves: 

➡️ $2.4 trillion – the estimated annual cost of dirty cooking in terms of healthcare, environmental degradation, and lost productivity. 

➡️ $2.5 billion - the total annual investment currently going into clean cooking solutions. That’s not even a third of what’s needed to achieve universal access by 2030. 

This is not an “investment gap.” It’s a missed opportunity to align climate, health, gender equity, and economic development goals through a single intervention. To change the trajectory, we need to shift the financing paradigm. Here are three catalytic approaches leading the way: 

1️⃣ Blended finance: Combining grants, guarantees, and concessional capital to de-risk private investment, reduce end-user costs, and help early-stage enterprises scale. 

2️⃣ Digital pay-as-you-go systems: Leveraging mobile payments and smart tech to improve affordability, enable real-time monitoring, and unlock access to carbon and impact finance. 

3️⃣ Outcome-based financing: Linking investor returns directly to measurable social and health results, shifting focus from inputs to verified impact. 

At UNDP, we’re advancing these models through Financial Innovation Labs, turning clean cooking from a development afterthought into core climate and infrastructure investment opportunities. Let’s de-risk, digitize, and diversify. Clean cooking is not a side issue; it's a frontline solution for sustainable development.  

#EnergyforDevelopment #CleanCooking

posts.caption:
No one should have to risk their health to cook a meal. Everyday, over 2.1 billion people strain over open fires and inhale smoke just to feed their families. The energy conversation isn’t complete without clean cooking.
 
This is not just about energy, it is a development priority. It’s about health, gender equality, economic opportunity, and climate action.
 
In sub-Saharan Africa alone, nearly 1 billion people lack access to clean cooking - and 20 million more fall behind every year. In Ethiopia, studies show that a 40% subsidy is often needed just to make biogas affordable. Yet infrastructure barriers like limited grid access and LPG distribution make electric and gas stoves unfeasible for many rural and displaced communities. To scale these technologies meaningfully, it is estimated that we need need at least +$4.5 billion annually - compared to the $700 million currently received.
 
But there’s a way forward. Imagine embedding clean cooking into data-driven electrification planning, so that every new grid, mini-grid or appliance rollout simultaneously advances clean cooking:
 
➡️ In Eswatini, minigrids are supporting productive uses and energy-efficient appliances to boost project revenues.
 
➡️ In Zambia, policy roadmaps link electric cooking with productive uses like irrigation and refrigeration.
 
➡️ In Ghana, Haiti, Kenya, Nepal, and Tanzania, pilots show that integrating electric cooking early in minigrid planning improves business viability.
 
Together, we can move clean cooking from the sidelines to the center of global energy and development strategies.
